caption: 01 · SIGNATURE — Why does one name dominate?. A single name gives press, commerce, and memory a compact handle. It can truthfully identify creative authority while still concealing the distributed labor required to materialize that authority.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping why does one name dominate? within The Myth of the Lone Fashion Genius.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 02 · CONSTELLATION — Who translated the idea?. Build a role map from concept to archive. Record not only names but decisions: who interpreted proportion, solved construction, negotiated feasibility, shaped the image, and preserved the evidence.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping who translated the idea? within The Myth of the Lone Fashion Genius.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 03 · CREDIT — What should the record retain?. Credits should travel with garments, images, video, collection notes, and archival deposits. The durable record needs consistent role language and a correction path when work is omitted or misdescribed.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping what should the record retain? within The Myth of the Lone Fashion Genius.
rights: Original publication graphic; no third-party imagery

crop: native 4:5 diagram; preserve labels and evidence footer
caption: 04 · POWER — Does visibility follow value?. Credit cannot by itself repair inequitable pay, ownership, or authority. It does, however, make labor and decision structures more legible—creating evidence for harder questions about compensation and control.
credit: Concept and editorial design: RN Collins
alt: Diagram mapping does visibility follow value? within The Myth of the Lone Fashion Genius.
